displayPattern: Washer display shows 9C1 (also shown as 9C2, PF, 3E, 2E, 9E1, 9E2, UC, 19C1 or 19C2 on some models)
meaning: Power supply (voltage) error: there is an irregularity in the electrical current reaching the washer.
causes: The washer shares its circuit with other loads instead of having its own
The washer is plugged into an extension cord
PF only: the power went out before the washer powered itself off (an outage, the washer being unplugged, or a tripped breaker)
A washer used outside its country of origin, where power grids and regulations differ
On some models 3E means a motor error, not a power supply error
diySteps: Confirm the washer is on its own circuit
Plug it straight into the wall outlet, not into an extension cord
If PF appeared after a power cut, an unplugged cord or a tripped breaker, that is what the code is reporting: power was lost before the washer switched itself off

If your display shows 3E, check your user manual to see whether it is a power supply error or a motor error. For a motor error Samsung's basic steps are to power off for 2 to 3 minutes, power back on and restart the cycle
If the code continues, request Samsung service
safetyNote: Unplug the washer (or switch off its breaker) and close the water taps before you reach behind it, handle hoses or open a filter. Water left from a recent hot cycle can be very hot, so let it cool first. Never bypass the door lock. Motor, pump, valve, sensor and control-board repairs belong to a qualified appliance technician.
proAdvice: Samsung says to request service if the code continues after the washer is on its own circuit without an extension cord.
